chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Aban ibn Uthman and al-Husayn ibn Abi Yusuf, from Abdul Malik ibn Amr, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is permissible for the man from the woman while she is menstruating?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Everything except the front private part.' He then said: 'Indeed, the woman is the toy of the man.'

key_terms.الْفَرْجُ: The private part (specifically the vagina in this context)

ai.seo_question: What acts are permissible between a husband and wife during menstruation according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of all sexual acts except vaginal intercourse during menstruation, a ruling derived from the general phrase 'everything except the farj' (private part). The concluding statement, 'The woman is the toy of the man,' is interpreted by Shia scholars not merely as a sign of dominance but as an indication of the husband's broad discretion and authority in utilizing his wife for pleasure within the bounds of the prohibition, reflecting a nuanced view of marital rights and intimacy.
